annotations.title: Where are the adults diagnosed with this condition, and how many?

description: Currently switched off: it answers "not available" and charges nothing. Use when the user is sizing a healthcare market, choosing where to put a clinic, a sales territory or clinical education, or diligencing a target's operating footprint: "which Texas counties have the most adults with diabetes?", "where is COPD most common in Ohio?". Returns CDC PLACES modelled prevalence for every county or place in the state, the spread across them, the areas holding the largest derived adult counts with the top-10 share, and a national benchmark. These are model estimates built from self-reported survey answers: diagnosed prevalence, not prevalence, and the adult counts are derived from the percentage rather than counted. The run says so in its own output, and says nothing about whether those adults are adequately treated. Refuses before you are charged if the measure matches nothing, matches more than one condition, or the rows fail their bounds. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Dimensions (vary these inputs to cut the answer; each call is its own run): over time: one release, one data year: PLACES is annual and two releases are not a trend; place: state, and level (county or place); segment: measure_id or condition (one of the 40 PLACES measures), type (crude or age_adjusted). For who is running trials in the condition, use run_trial_pipeline; for how many households match a profile in one area, use run_audience_size.

condition.description: A phrase matched against the measure name, e.g. "coronary heart disease". Give this or measure_id. Refuses if it matches more than one measure.

level.description: County (default) or place (incorporated and census-designated places).

measure_id.description: A PLACES measure id, e.g. "DIABETES", "BPHIGH", "COPD", "CHD", "CASTHMA", "DEPRESSION". Give this or condition.

state.description: A two-letter US state or DC code, e.g. "TX".

top.description: Areas to list in each ranking. Default 15.

type.description: Crude (default) is the share of that area's own adults and is what a headcount needs. Age-adjusted removes the area's age mix and is for comparing areas, not for multiplying by a population.
